items.quote: return not mask or mask == 0 or (bit and math.floor(mask / bit) % 2 == 1)
items.what: The local Matches in Window.GuideOutline (UI/WindowGuide.lua:31-33) re-implements Model.HasBit (Planning/Model.lua:38-42, the canonical home, already exported and used by UI/Hints/Hearth.lua:36 and Integrations/Dungeons.lua:24-25); call ns.Model.HasBit and delete Matches.
items.why: rg 'HasBit|math.floor\(.*/.*\) % 2' over the repo: Model.HasBit is `not mask or mask == 0 or (bit > 0 and math.floor(mask / bit) % 2 == 1)`; Matches is the same expression with `bit and` in place of `bit > 0`. The one difference: Matches guards a nil bit and HasBit guards a zero bit; for the integers the type allows both return the same result (a zero bit never matches a non-zero mask in either). AGFPlayer.raceBit/classBit are typed integer (types/Namespace.lua:107-108), never nil, so the swap preserves behaviour. The surrounding side/race/class filter at lines 36-39 is also the third statement of the permanent character restriction (Model.lua:396-401 SimpleOpen, Integrations/Dungeons.lua:20-27 Dungeons.ForCharacter), each written slightly differently (ForCharacter treats any side other than 1 or 2 as open and a zero player bit as matching).
items.reason: Matches is a two-line guard covered by the parallel-implementations lens's small-idiom exclusion. The broader filters serve different contracts: Dungeons.ForCharacter allows unknown player bits, while GuideOutline and Model.SimpleOpen exclude restricted quests.

items.quote: card.ShowButton = button
items.what: card.ShowButton is fully dead; remove the stored alias and its field annotation, keeping the button itself.
items.why: Whole-repository searches, including tests, tools, hidden configuration, workflows, docs, XML, generated data and available host annotations, find only this assignment and the annotation at line 32. Dynamic dispatch: Window.CreateCard constructs a plain unnamed Button without a template or mixin; the shared Overview.CardClick/CardTooltip/RefreshCardTooltip handlers do not inspect this field, and no string-built lookup can select ShowButton. Dump.KeyIn enumerates only the actual parent: this button belongs to the inner content frame, whereas the alias is stored on its grandparent card, so removing the alias cannot change its dump path. Public surface/cross-boundary: this local card field is not a documented integration API or exported entrypoint. Manifests/ops and data-driven lookup: the TOC, Panel.xml, Bindings.xml, packaging, scripts, CI and docs supply no consumer; the field is not persisted or registered. Open work: git grep across all 117 local and remote-tracking refs finds only the same assignment and annotation; no additional in-flight branch was specified. No dead-code hard stop applies. The parent retains the live button and its OnClick closure, and the following anchors use the local button directly. window_spec (147 checks) and guide_ui_spec (157 checks) pass both normally and with only this assignment removed in memory across 25 addon loads.

items.quote: card.journey, card.state = journey, "shown"
items.what: BUG: WindowJourneys.lua:192 always labels the selected journey "shown", drifting from Panel.lua:1159 and the canonical chosen-card behavior in Overview.CardClick (Overview.lua:304-323).
items.why: WindowJourneys.lua:179-180 attaches the shared CardClick/CardTooltip handlers, but RefreshCard never sets "chosen" even when Refresh computes chosen=true at line 383. Panel supplies "chosen" for the active journey. Overview.CardClick uses that state to refocus an already-running journey without calling ns.Choose, or resume it when paused; "shown" instead calls ns.Choose(key, titleStartsRoute). With the default titleStartsRoute=true, Core.lua:712 and 791-792 restart guidance through StartRoute. A read-only stdin LuaJIT reproduction using tests/harness.lua, spf="v1+", completed={844}, and log quests 845 (complete) and 843 selected the route and then clicked its visible window card: route.chosen=true, card.state="shown", ns.Choose called once, and NavigateRoute increased 1 -> 2. Clicking the map panel chosen card immediately afterward left NavigateRoute at 2; the harness reported zero errors. The same state also makes the selected window card tooltip say CLICK_TO_CHOOSE. The window intentionally keeps the large-card layout, but that visual choice should not change the shared click/tooltip contract. Found while comparing the parallel map/window implementations; fixing this changes behavior and is not a cleanup-only edit.
items.reason: window cards take the chosen state for the chosen journey, as the map panel's do, so a second click never restarts guidance

items.quote: card.journey, card.state = journey, "shown"
items.what: BUG: the selected window card is always marked shown, making the shared handler's chosen-card branches unreachable and restarting active guidance on a click.
items.why: RefreshCard sets this state for both the featured card and grid cards, including when Refresh has established route.chosen and first.key == route.journey (lines 383-396). CreateCard wires Overview.CardClick and Overview.CardTooltip at lines 179-180. Overview.lua:304-329 uses self.state == "chosen" to preserve an active route or resume a paused one; "shown" always calls ns.Choose again.
